input: The exact checked field model, complete Entity and Value Object factory bindings, and current generated Rust Rule modules.
output: Private-field owned Rust values, public borrowed getters, owned input carriers, structured validation failure, and factory values that bind every declared base and additive extension Rule before construction.
entity: Entity PartialEq, Eq and Hash are implemented manually over the declared identity field only. Construction and lifecycle snapshots retain identity and return immutable owned values.
value_object: Value Object PartialEq, Eq and Hash cover every declared normalized field. Nested owned values retain their own native equality contract.
validation: Factories run base Rules first in declared order, then enabled additive extensions in declared extension and validator order. Any failure returns codes and no formed value. Value Object base validators exactly cover invariant references.
ownership: Factory create consumes its input only after validation. It moves values into the immutable result and does not clone across concept boundaries. Getters borrow fields.
references: Checked identity-reference and field-projection bindings are emitted as inert qualified metadata. They do not load, dereference or assert target existence.
failure: Missing validators, incomplete bindings, wrong field paths or types, duplicate Rules/extensions, invalid identifiers, stale inputs and output collisions reject during planning. Native invalid values return a typed validation error.
effects: Planning and generated formation are pure; there is no I/O, persistence, environment access or provider invocation.
